values.name: Tier 1 metro (Mumbai / Delhi / Bengaluru / Chennai / Hyderabad / Kolkata / Ahmedabad / Pune)

facts.text: The government classes 8 cities as X (Tier 1) for house rent allowance, the highest rate: Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Ahmedabad and Pune. Rents and prices are highest here.
Urban Indians spend on average ₹6,996 per person per month (2023-24), about 70% more than rural Indians (₹4,122).

values.name: Tier 2 city (e.g. Jaipur / Lucknow / Nagpur / Indore / Kochi)

facts.text: About 97 cities are classed Y (Tier 2) by the government, with lower living costs than the 8 metros.
Urban Indians spend on average ₹6,996 per person per month (2023-24), about 70% more than rural Indians (₹4,122).
All cities not classed X or Y are Z class (Tier 3), with the lowest house rent allowance.
Urban Indians spend on average ₹6,996 per person per month (2023-24), about 70% more than rural Indians (₹4,122).
Rural Indians spend on average ₹4,122 per person per month (2023-24); the rural-urban gap has narrowed from 84% in 2011-12 to about 70%.

india_income_tiers.title: India income tiers (household, Tier 1 to Tier 4)

segments.name: Tier 1: rich household (over ₹30 lakh a year)

facts.text: Rich households (over ₹30 lakh a year) spend about ₹20.5 lakh a year on average, about 3 times a middle-class household (ICE 360 survey, 2020-21 prices).

segments.name: Tier 2: middle-class household (₹5 to 30 lakh a year)

facts.text: Middle-class households (₹5 to 30 lakh a year) spend about ₹6.9 lakh a year on average and were about 31% of households in 2021 (ICE 360 survey).

segments.name: Tier 3: aspiring household (₹1.25 to 5 lakh a year)

facts.text: Aspirer households earn ₹1.25 to 5 lakh a year (ICE 360 survey classes); much of the budget goes on food, housing and essentials.

segments.name: Tier 4: low-income household (under ₹1.25 lakh a year)

facts.text: The lowest-income households (under ₹1.25 lakh a year) spend about ₹82,300 a year on average, mostly on food and shelter (ICE 360 survey).

uk_london.title: London vs rest of the UK

facts.text: London had the highest spending per person of the English regions in 2023 (£28,600) and the highest household saving ratio (23.9%).
Spending per person across English regions ranged from £19,842 (North East) to £28,600 (London) in 2023.
